stem: The graph of $f(\theta)={=a}\sin\theta {=signed(q)}$ is drawn for $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le360^{\circ}$. What is the amplitude of $f$?
solution: For $f(\theta)=a\sin\theta+q$ the amplitude is $|a|$: the distance from the middle line $y=q$ up to the maximum (or down to the minimum). It is never negative, and $q$ only moves the graph up or down, so it does not change the amplitude.
notes: Entry point: read a off the equation. a is negative in half of the instances (the book's own f(x) = -sin x + 2 has amplitude 1, not -1) and q is always non-zero so the equation prints with a sign. Answer is |a|; q is the decoy. Params give 100 distinct instances.
